subject: Re: Coordinating 90-min architecture deep dive across US/EU/APAC

From: Alexei Ivanov <alexei.ivanov@auroratech.com>

Cc: Claire Dupont <claire.dupont@auroratech.eu>, Kenji Sato <k.sato@auroratech.jp>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:20:00 +0100
Subject: Coordinating a 90-min architecture deep dive with Redwood

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. AuroraTech's platform team would like to get a focused 90-minute technical deep dive with one of your solutions engineers to go over: model selection and quantization tradeoffs, network egress and VPC routing options for Private deployments, and expected token-latency at our typical sequence lengths.

Attendees (anticipated):
- Alexei Ivanov (AuroraTech, EU/PM)
- Claire Dupont (AuroraTech, EU/Platform Architect)
- Kenji Sato (AuroraTech, APAC/Infra Architect)
- Marcus Lin (Redwood SE) — if available
- Priya Natarajan (Redwood AM) — coordinating

We need to be mindful of two constraints: 1) our APAC architect (Kenji) is in JST and prefers finishing by 23:30 local time, and 2) some of our US engineering leadership will be offline for the Thanksgiving holiday (Nov 26–27).

Proposed date windows (local times shown):
- Option A: Dec 1 — 09:00–10:30 PST / 17:00–18:30 CET / 01:00–02:30 JST (Dec 2 JST)
- Option B: Dec 3 — 07:30–09:00 PST / 15:30–17:00 CET / 23:30–01:00 JST

Can you confirm Marcus's availability for either option or suggest two 90-min UTC windows that work for Redwood? If possible, please attach a simple availability grid so we can mark confirmed slots. Also flag any materials we should prepare (network diagrams, expected QPS, sample prompts).

Thanks — we want to lock this in by the end of the week.

Best,
Alexei
AuroraTech
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>

Alexei — thanks for the detail and the constraints, noted on Thanksgiving and Kenji's cutoff. Attaching a quick availability grid (aurora-availability-grid.xlsx) that maps the candidate slots into UTC so it's easier to compare.

A few notes on the options you proposed and two canonical UTC windows we can commit to from Redwood's side (Marcus is copied):

- Option A (Dec 1): 17:00–18:30 CET (your local) = 16:00–17:30 UTC — Marcus says he can do Dec 1 16:00–17:30 UTC but that puts Kenji at 01:00 JST (just after his preferred cutoff).
- Option B (Dec 3): 15:30–17:00 CET = 14:30–16:00 UTC — that maps to 23:30–01:00 JST, which is tight for Kenji.

Proposed Redwood candidate windows (UTC, pick one):
1) Dec 1, 16:00–17:30 UTC (works for Marcus; APAC will be late)
2) Dec 2, 14:00–15:30 UTC (a bit earlier for EU, more friendly for APAC — Kenji would be at 23:00 JST)

Ask: please confirm the final attendee list (Marcus will want access to network contacts for any firewall/egress questions ahead of the call) and whether we should run a 10–15 minute pre-call with your infra team to exchange diagram PDFs.

I attached the availability grid and a blank meeting agenda template. If you confirm window #2 (Dec 2, 14:00–15:30 UTC) I can send a calendar invite in UTC with the recording and follow-up notes plan.

On quoting your note about holidays — happy to avoid Nov 26–27 for any leadership-level approvals.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0124

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear UTC options and for doing the conversion.

Quick reply to confirm preferences from the Aurora side:
- Marcus (SE) being present is important — thanks for looping him in.
- Kenji is willing to stretch to 23:00 JST but anything later risks degraded focus; he prefers Dec 2 if possible.
- Our EU architects (myself and Alexei) can do Dec 2, 14:00–15:30 UTC without issues.

So, leaning strongly to Redwood's candidate window #2 (Dec 2, 14:00–15:30 UTC). A couple of quick asks:
- Can Marcus prepare a short slide (5–7 slides) on latency-by-quantization and a one-slide runbook for fallback routing?
- We'll send a network diagram PDF in advance (Claire -> Priya) — please confirm the best secure upload location (we prefer a short-lived link).

Thanks for accommodating the Thanksgiving window — appreciate the flexibility.
